## Anscombe's Quartet {.smaller}

[Why we visualize]{.eyebrow}

### Same statistics, different shapes

:::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::: columns
:::: {.column width="45%"}
Four datasets with identical statistics:

- Same means
- Same variance
- Same correlation (0.816)
- Same regression line

::: {.fragment .fade-in}
**Why does this matter?**

Anscombe's Quartet shows why plotting data is essential — summary statistics alone can hide crucial patterns.
:::
::::

::: {.column width="55%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 5

anscombe = load_anscombe()

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(6, 5), constrained_layout=True)
for ax, (dataset, group) in zip(axes.flat, anscombe.groupby('dataset')):
    ax.scatter(group['x'], group['y'], color=GREEN, s=60, alpha=0.75, zorder=3)
    m, b = np.polyfit(group['x'], group['y'], 1)
    xs = np.linspace(group['x'].min(), group['x'].max(), 100)
    ax.plot(xs, m * xs + b, color=PURPLE, linewidth=1.8, zorder=2)
    ax.set_title(f'Dataset {dataset}', fontsize=11)
    ax.set_xlabel('x'); ax.set_ylabel('y')
fig.suptitle("Anscombe's Quartet", fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
plt.show()
```
:::
::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::

::: {.footer style="font-size: 0.55em; color: #808080; white-space: nowrap;"}
Source: Anscombe, F. J. (1973). Graphs in Statistical Analysis. *The American Statistician*, 27(1), 17–21.
:::

## The Datasaurus Dozen {.smaller}

[Why we visualize]{.eyebrow}

### Identical stats, different shapes

All 13 datasets have nearly identical summary statistics but vastly different shapes!

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: center

# Load the real Datasaurus Dozen from the course package — carefully
# constructed datasets that share identical summary statistics but look
# completely different.
dd = load_datasaurus()

order = ["dino", "away", "h_lines", "v_lines", "x_shape",
         "star", "high_lines", "dots", "circle", "bullseye",
         "slant_up", "slant_down", "wide_lines"]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 5, figsize=(13, 6.2),
                         constrained_layout=True,
                         facecolor="white")
for ax, name in zip(axes.flat, order):
    grp = dd[dd["dataset"] == name]
    ax.scatter(grp["x"], grp["y"],
               color=COLORS["primary"], s=10, alpha=0.75, linewidths=0)
    ax.set_title(name, fontsize=9, fontweight="bold",
                 color=COLORS["text_dark"])
    ax.set_facecolor("white")
    ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
    for spine in ax.spines.values():
        spine.set_visible(False)

# We have 13 datasets in a 3×5 grid → hide the last two empty cells
axes.flat[13].set_visible(False)
axes.flat[14].set_visible(False)

# Add a summary-stats panel in the empty corner
stats = (dd.groupby("dataset")
           .agg(mean_x=("x","mean"), mean_y=("y","mean"),
                sd_x=("x","std"),    sd_y=("y","std"))
           .round(2))
ax_text = fig.add_subplot(3, 5, 15)
ax_text.axis("off")
ax_text.text(0.0, 0.95,
             "All 13 datasets share:",
             fontsize=10, fontweight="bold", color=COLORS["text_dark"],
             transform=ax_text.transAxes)
ax_text.text(0.0, 0.70,
             f"x̄ ≈ {stats['mean_x'].mean():.1f}\n"
             f"ȳ ≈ {stats['mean_y'].mean():.1f}\n"
             f"σx ≈ {stats['sd_x'].mean():.1f}\n"
             f"σy ≈ {stats['sd_y'].mean():.1f}",
             fontsize=10, color=COLORS["text_mid"], family="monospace",
             transform=ax_text.transAxes, va="top")

fig.suptitle("THE DATASAURUS DOZEN — IDENTICAL STATS, DIFFERENT SHAPES",
             fontsize=13, fontweight="bold", color=COLORS["text_dark"])
plt.show()
```

::: {.footer style="font-size: 0.55em; color: #808080; white-space: nowrap;"}
Source: Matejka & Fitzmaurice (2017). [Same Stats, Different Graphs](https://www.research.autodesk.com/publications/same-stats-different-graphs/). ACM CHI 2017.
:::
